clue.text: Skill that guarantees one a good hand

definitions.text: Skill that guarantees one a good hand

parts.words: Skill that guarantees one a good hand
parts.note: a good hand reads like luck at cards or a helper, but here it is neat handwriting, and the skill is that of writing well

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a talent that always deals them winning cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good hand' suggests card games; the hand meant is a person's handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of writing by hand is judged by the quality of one's script, so mastering it secures neat handwriting.

clue.text: Choose examination for this sort of college

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student picks an exam to get into a particular college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College' suggests a university, but it is the body of electors that chooses the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: The US president is formally chosen by a body of state electors, a voting college.

clue.text: Criminals with family values

parts.note: family values sounds wholesome, but these gangsters are organised into crime families

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers claim to be traditional and moral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian-rooted crime syndicate is organised into 'families', so its gangsters prize the family.

clue.text: Is going into subtle distinctions lots of bother?

indicators.note: going into means entering, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: nuances are subtle distinctions or shades of meaning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether examining fine shades of meaning is troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural irritations or pests make up a great deal of annoyance.

clue.text: Part of leg and most of rump of small creature

parts.note: the ham is the back of the thigh

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: the stern is the rear or rump

explanation.surface: A butcher describes cuts of leg and rump from a little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final N of STERN, leaving STER.
explanation.definitionFit: The rodent kept as a pet is a little furry animal.

clue.text: Echo in prison cell

annotationWithheld.why: Echo in prison cell (5), PETER: 'prison cell' defines it (slang), but 'Echo in' gives no wordplay for PETER and no parse found

clue.text: Sweetheart, an old and faithful partner

parts.note: jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart or darling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover is described as a long-standing, loyal companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to 'Darby and Joan', the proverbial devoted elderly couple; 'an' does double duty only in the surface, here it simply gives AN.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase Darby and Joan she is the loyal elderly wife of a long marriage.

clue.text: Establishing connections and becoming a member

definitions.meaning: linking things together, as of pipes or wires
enrolling in a club or the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: Linking pieces together is connecting them, and enlisting in a society is enrolling.

clue.text: So long in an isolated state

definitions.text: So long in an isolated state

parts.words: So long in an isolated state
parts.note: so long is a farewell, and the isolated state is Hawaii, far out in the Pacific, where this greeting is used

explanation.surface: Someone has lived alone for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like a length of time; it is a goodbye, and the remote state is Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word serves as both hello and goodbye in that remote Pacific state.

clue.text: Again declare concern about a fellow at the front

indicators.note: these words place the pieces before the word for a concern rather than after it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a concern is a business, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone restates their worry about a man leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like part of the surface worry, but it means a business, FIRM, and 'at the front' puts RE, A and F ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something once more is to restate or confirm it anew.

clue.text: Remove end or adapt for special purpose

parts.note: to tail fruit or vegetables is to cut off the end, as in 'top and tail'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions offer a choice between trimming something or reworking it for a specific use.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a double definition with 'or' as a link, but 'or' supplies its own letters after TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something fit a particular need is to customise it, as a cutter fits a suit to a client.

clue.text: Outrageous articles about Western capital

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous or excessive

indicators.note: the two articles go around the letter for Western, enclosing it

parts.note: a and a are two indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Shocking newspaper pieces concern a western city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper stories but means the grammatical article A, twice; 'about' puts the pair around W to make AWA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the seat of the Canadian government, the national capital city.

clue.text: For example, Victoria's time at home with Albert

parts.note: a term is a period of time
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
Al is a short form of the name Albert

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria's period of domestic life with Prince Albert is recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria and Albert suggest the royal couple, but Victoria is the London railway station; read 'Victoria's' as 'Victoria is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a London railway station where lines end, an example of a terminus.

clue.text: Snatch king and jack

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, stands for King George
a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with two playing cards, a king and a jack.
explanation.walkthrough: King and jack suggest playing cards; here they are GR and the sailor AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize something quickly is to snatch it.

clue.text: For a change, potentially a novel present?

definitions.text: For a change, potentially a novel present?

parts.words: For a change, potentially a novel present?
parts.note: the gift is a voucher a shop will exchange for any title, so it may become a work of fiction

explanation.surface: Someone suggests giving an original gift for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a change' and 'novel' seem to mean 'unusually' and 'new'; the gift voucher is exchanged for a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher redeemable at a bookshop is a gift card that buys reading matter.

clue.text: Creator of religious works holds a vicar agog with excitement

indicators.note: excitement stirs the letters up, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist's work grips an enthralled clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' is only a link here; the anagram of A VICAR AGOG gives the Italian Baroque painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Baroque master painted many biblical scenes, such as The Calling of Saint Matthew.

clue.text: Vehicle with insurance going round university city

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the cover surrounds the letter

parts.note: cover is insurance protection

explanation.surface: A van with its insurance travels around a university town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts COVER around U to give COUVER.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large port city in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: Dissembling in vain, since revealed

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone's pretence proves futile, since it has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' looks like the hidden indicator but is fodder: the letters run from vaIN SINCE REvealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hides true feelings behind a false front is being hypocritical.

clue.text: Possible murder clue revealed in no tabloids, oddly

indicators.note: behaving oddly suggests the letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Evidence from a killing is reported somewhere other than the popular press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed in' only links the definition to the anagram; 'oddly' rearranges NO TABLOIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of blood at a crime scene is the sort of evidence detectives follow.

clue.text: Hard-hearted Roman general identifying solitary saint

indicators.note: having something at the heart puts it into the middle of the other word

parts.note: Mark Antony was a Roman general
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough Roman commander is identified with a hermit saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-hearted' reads as cruel but puts H at the heart of ANTONY; 'identifying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Anthony of Egypt was a desert hermit, the father of monasticism.

clue.text: Pretentious sounding bunch of flowers

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken rather than spelt, so it is a homophone

parts.note: posey means pretentious or affected

explanation.surface: A showy bouquet is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bouquet, often of garden blooms, is a nosegay.

clue.text: Try to fish using a singularly useless bit of wood

parts.note: to cast is to try, as in casting about for something, or casting a line
to net is to catch fish with a mesh, so fishing using one gives this verb

explanation.surface: An angler tries a net, which proves a useless piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: These clappers come in pairs, so one alone is 'singularly useless'; together the pieces read 'cast a net', what you do when trying to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish percussion instrument is a pair of shells, so a single one cannot be clicked.

clue.text: From the beginning, not quite superior to second in command

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: above means superior to or higher than

indicators.note: second in picks the second letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An officer is almost senior to the deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second in command' looks like a deputy; it is the second letter of 'command', O; 'not quite' cuts ABOVE to ABOV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means literally 'from the egg', from the very start.

clue.text: Made a record that's famous

definitions.meaning: wrote something down as a record

explanation.definitionFit: Writing something down is recording it, and a celebrated person is renowned.

clue.text: Sang, or otherwise used musical instruments

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choir either sang or played their instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe instruments played from keyboards in churches are keyboard instruments.

clue.text: Express awe about king's understanding

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to gasp is to express awe
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a monarch's comprehension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GASP around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Comprehension of a subject is a firm hold on it, a mental grip.

clue.text: Isolated area that may be picked by thief

definitions.text: that may be picked by thief
definitions.meaning: a pickpocket steals from the pouch sewn into clothing

explanation.definitionFit: A pouch in clothing is what a pickpocket picks, and a small separate area is a pocket of something.

clue.text: Avoid bet that's silly and done away with

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foolish wager to shun has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a need or difficulty is to make it unnecessary, to prevent or eliminate it.

clue.text: Constable, for example, or a Welsh painter

definitions.meaning: the English landscape painter Constable had this first name
Augustus, the Welsh portraitist, had this surname

explanation.definitionFit: The landscape artist Constable was christened with this name, and the Welsh portraitist Augustus bore it as a surname.

clue.text: No room in hotel for this visitor?

definitions.text: No room in hotel for this visitor?

parts.words: No room in hotel for this visitor?
parts.note: a hotel with no vacancies suggests an unlucky guest, but this visitor never needs a bed since they go home the same evening

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the hotel fully booked.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursionist travels out and back within one day, so needs no overnight lodging.
